- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.

# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto, titled "For a Fair Deal," outlines policies across five key themes.

## Economy
The party proposes investing in renewable energy and home insulation to reduce energy bills while creating jobs. They plan to reform business rates, support small businesses through expanded British Business Bank functions, and introduce Lifelong Skills Grants for adult education. They advocate repairing trade relationships with Europe and responsible fiscal management.

## Public Services
Healthcare reforms include guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases), recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, and improving NHS dental access. Mental health provisions would expand through community hubs and school-based professionals. Cancer treatment guarantees and increased public health investment are proposed.

Social care reforms include introducing free personal care, creating a National Care Agency, and establishing a Royal College of Care Workers with higher minimum wages. Unpaid carers would receive increased Carer's Allowance and respite break guarantees.

Education proposals include mental health professionals in every school, increased per-pupil funding, maintenance grants for disadvantaged students, and a tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils.

## Environment
Environmental policies centre on ending sewage pollution by transforming water companies into public benefit companies and banning executive bonuses until pollution ends. They propose achieving 90% renewable electricity by 2030, net zero by 2045, and launching emergency home insulation programmes. Nature restoration targets include doubling protected areas and planting 60 million trees annually.

## Housing and Communities
Housing commitments include building 380,000 homes annually (150,000 social homes), banning no-fault evictions, creating three-year default tenancies, and abolishing residential leasehold. Local authorities would gain powers to control second homes and set planning fees.

## Immigration and Asylum
Immigration reforms would end the "Hostile Environment" policy, scrap the Rwanda scheme, and establish a three-month service standard for asylum decisions. Work visa policy would transfer to relevant departments, and asylum seekers could work after three months.

## Democracy and Rights
Political reforms include introducing proportional representation for MPs and English councillors, giving 16-17 year olds voting rights, capping political donations, and enshrining the Ministerial Code in law. The Human Rights Act would be protected, and a comprehensive Race Equality Strategy implemented.

## Defence and International
Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP with army cuts reversed. International priorities include supporting Ukraine, returning aid to 0.7% of national income, and pursuing closer EU relations through a four-stage roadmap ultimately aiming for Single Market membership.
